method: Every candidate that passed automated scoring was then viewed as an image. Filename scoring alone let through a scanned book, a Project Blue Book PDF and a WWII-era portrait, so nothing here is accepted on a name match.

reject.2: scanned book of portraits, not a photograph of a place
reject.3: archival B&W of the Linden Towers gates, demolished 1936
reject.4: vague B&W survey landscape, subject not identifiable
reject.6: the 1915 Southern Pacific depot, not the Burlingame Park neighborhood
reject.7: a scanned Project Blue Book PDF that happens to name Cupertino
reject.8: indoor political event at De Anza College, wrong subject and dates badly
reject.10: correct subject (Clark House) but archival B&W sits wrong on a current listing page
reject.14: the Mills estate, demolished in 1954 - not today's Mills Estates neighborhood
reject.15: Dorothea Lange portrait of a named farmer, WWII incarceration era; wrong subject and not ours to repurpose
reject.19: a decorated utility box on a Temescal sidewalk; right place, unusable image
reject.27: San Bruno Mountain, not the San Bruno Park neighborhood
